title: The future of warfare? (from my email) - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: An anonymous reader emailed Cowen a compact thesis: as weapons get better they will target each other rather than people, lowering casualties and therefore making wars easier to start and harder to end; warfare shifts from industrial to techno-industrial, current low-tech/high-tech parity is an artifact of non-deployment, and necessity-driven blocs will fight near-continuously at varying intensity.

themes.theme: Machine-vs-machine war lowers the entry barrier

insights.claim: As weapon systems improve they will increasingly target each other rather than humans, and the resulting drop in casualties will make it easier for states to enter conflicts and harder for them to exit.
insights.so_what: If casualty aversion is the main brake on conflict, removing it raises the baseline frequency and duration of war — a structural bid for defense spending and a risk premium on global trade.
insights.quote: As weapon systems increase in effectiveness, they will generally target one another rather than humans. Lower loss of life will ease conflict entry and hinder exit.
insights.locator: As weapon systems increase in effectiveness
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen

insights.claim: Blocs are expected to engage in near-constant warfare across varying intensity levels rather than in discrete wars separated by peace.
insights.so_what: Persistent low-grade conflict is a different regime from episodic war: it structurally elevates defense budgets, insurance and logistics costs.
insights.quote: Blocs may well engage in near constant warfare of various intensity levels.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen

insights.claim: The apparent parity between low-tech and advanced military actors is an artifact of advanced systems being deployed at near-zero scale, and that parity will disappear once those systems are actually fielded.
insights.so_what: Cheap-drone-beats-expensive-platform conclusions drawn from recent conflicts may be a sampling artifact; do not extrapolate them into procurement theses.
insights.quote: the current appearance of parity between low tech and advanced actors reflects near zero deployment of advanced systems
insights.locator: Warfare will veer further from industrial competition
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen

insights.claim: Warfare is shifting from industrial competition — who can mass-produce materiel — to techno-industrial competition, in which technological sophistication combined with production capacity is decisive.
insights.so_what: Reframes defense competitiveness around advanced manufacturing and human capital rather than raw output — favors economies with both.
insights.quote: Warfare will veer further from industrial competition into techno-industrial
insights.locator: Warfare will veer further from industrial competition
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen

themes.theme: Blocs, logistics and the value of inputs

insights.claim: Because no single state can supply an advanced military ecosystem alone, alliances will form around the need to pool human capital, techno-industrial capacity, and material inputs.
insights.so_what: Alliance formation becomes a supply-chain problem, which predicts realignments that cut across current ideological groupings.
insights.quote: The need for advanced ecosystems will lead to blocs able to combine human capital, techno-industrial capacity, and inputs.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen

insights.claim: Contested logistics at elevated levels changes the incentives around geographic size and raises the value of raw inputs, since territory that once conferred depth may become a liability while input access becomes decisive.
insights.so_what: A structural argument for strategic-input scarcity pricing and for reshoring of critical materials, independent of current tariff politics.
insights.quote: Logistics may be contested at elevated levels, changing the incentives around geographic size and increasing the value of inputs.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen

insights.claim: Bloc membership will be driven by necessity rather than ideology and will therefore be more fluid, with states switching alignment as their input and capacity needs change.
insights.so_what: Treat alliance structures as repriceable rather than fixed — a source of geopolitical volatility that long-dated assumptions tend to miss.
insights.quote: Bloc composition will be necessity driven, perhaps with increased fluidity.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
